observations: A large skull outline occupies the center-left, and inside it sits a smaller nested face with two distinct features: a left eye rendered as a pink starburst surrounded by concentric orange and brown rings, and a right eye marked with a red cross on a yellow-brown ground.

A circular face with dot eyes and a row of bared teeth appears in the upper right against a field of yellow radiating lines, drawn at a noticeably smaller scale than the central skull and outlined in black.

A bright blue dashed line curves from the lower left up through the mid-ground, passing between the outer skull's jaw and a row of white rectangular teeth visible along the lower edge of the nested inner face.
reading: A skull contains a second face within it — the outer form providing the frame, the inner face carrying its own two eyes and expression. That nesting gives the image a sense of something enclosed or watched from inside. The smaller sun-like face in the corner reads as a separate presence, cooler in scale. The blue dashed line threads the gap between these forms, while purple ovals and white loops keep the dark ground restless.
contextAngle: In the owned nnotb subset, this work holds title number #0000 while its recorded-creation position sits at the opposite end of the sequence from nnotb #1 — an unusual pairing of first title and last recorded creation.

connections.reason: Both images build figures from nested outlines with visible teeth, but nnotb #1 distributes multiple forms across an open bright-blue field while nnotb #0000 compresses its nested structure into a dark, tightly packed ground.

lookingQuestion: Can you trace where the outer skull's boundary ends and the inner face's boundary begins — and does the blue dashed line stay inside or outside that threshold?
ambiguities: nnotb #87 contains lettering treated as content per instructions; no strong formal connection to #0000 was found, so it was omitted.
nifty-faces #0000 shares dense line-work but its forms are more architectural than figural, making the connection too loose to include.
